name: Jesher
overview: Jesher was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Cheubai, also known as Caleb. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional personal notes recorded. This positions him within the lineage of Judah, an important tribe in the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Jesher is a proper name that may mean 'the deity shows himself just,' reflecting a possible theological significance in its Hebrew meaning. This name was not given directly by God but carries a meaning that could imply divine justice or righteousness.
familyAndRelationships: Jesher is explicitly recorded as the son of Cheubai (Caleb) and also noted as the son of Azubah, indicating his immediate family ties. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Jesher's significance lies in his placement within the genealogical records of Judah, which are foundational for understanding the heritage of the Israelite tribes. Being a son of Cheubai (Caleb) ties him to a line that is important for the biblical history of Judah. Although his role is not elaborated upon, his inclusion in 1 Chronicles 2:18 affirms the continuity of God's covenantal promises through the tribe of Judah.
